clusters.brief:
# Draft: Low-altitude encounters and near-midair collision risk with unmanned aircraft systems (drones)

## Hazard
Manned aircraft operating at low altitudes or along airport approach corridors encounter unmanned aircraft systems (drones) in close proximity with little to no advance warning, requiring immediate visual identification and evasive maneuvers to prevent midair collisions. [ACN 1044401] [ACN 1461959] [ACN 1640441] [ACN 1748192] [ACN 1799467]

## Precedent
No comparable reports outside this cluster appear in this batch. [ACN 1044401] [ACN 1461959] [ACN 1640441] [ACN 1748192] [ACN 1799467]

## Risk Assessment
The deterministic risk calculation for this cluster consists of five member reports [ACN 1044401] [ACN 1461959] [ACN 1640441] [ACN 1748192] [ACN 1799467]:

* **Member Count (5):** The dataset contains 5 documented incident reports forming the basis of this cluster [ACN 1044401] [ACN 1461959] [ACN 1640441] [ACN 1748192] [ACN 1799467].
* **Severity (1.00):** The maximum score of 1.00 indicates that the incidents within this group reached the highest level of deterministic operational severity [ACN 1044401] [ACN 1461959] [ACN 1640441] [ACN 1748192] [ACN 1799467].
* **Frequency (0.25):** The frequency score of 0.25 represents a lower-to-moderate rate of occurrence relative to the broader reporting baseline, driven by the volume of 5 events [ACN 1044401] [ACN 1461959] [ACN 1640441] [ACN 1748192] [ACN 1799467].
* **Trend (0.70):** The trend value of 0.70 reflects an elevated, upward trajectory over time, showing an increasing pattern or recency among the reported events [ACN 1044401] [ACN 1461959] [ACN 1640441] [ACN 1748192] [ACN 1799467].
* **Total Risk (0.71):** The composite risk score of 0.71 is the mathematical aggregation of the maximum severity, baseline frequency, and positive trend calculated across all five member reports [ACN 1044401] [ACN 1461959] [ACN 1640441] [ACN 1748192] [ACN 1799467].

## Recommended Brief
Flight crews operating at low altitudes between approximately 500 and 1,200 feet AGL and along airport approach corridors have experienced close encounters with unmanned aircraft systems (drones) [ACN 1044401] [ACN 1461959] [ACN 1640441] [ACN 1748192] [ACN 1799467]. Because drones lacked transponder equipment to trigger onboard traffic alert systems, pilots received no electronic collision warnings and had only seconds of visual notice upon spotting the small aircraft [ACN 1044401] [ACN 1640441] [ACN 1748192] [ACN 1799467]. In multiple instances, pilots were forced to execute immediate flight-path deviations or sharp bank and pedal maneuvers to prevent collisions, while high closure rates in other encounters left no time for evasive action as drones passed within 60 to 200 feet [ACN 1044401] [ACN 1461959] [ACN 1640441] [ACN 1748192] [ACN 1799467]. Pilots operating on approach paths reported these drone sightings to air traffic control to alert and protect trailing traffic [ACN 1461959] [ACN 1748192].

# Draft: VFR Airborne Traffic Conflicts and Near Midair Collisions

## Hazard
General aviation aircraft operating in visual meteorological conditions experience near midair collisions and critical loss of separation with other aircraft, necessitating immediate evasive maneuvers (ACN 1111863, ACN 1470131, ACN 1490553). [ACN 1026406] [ACN 1111863] [ACN 1130209] [ACN 1295187] [ACN 1419324] [ACN 1470131] [ACN 1490553] [ACN 1699435] [ACN 1712248] [ACN 1851899]

## Precedent
Precedent analysis unavailable this run. [ACN 1026406] [ACN 1111863] [ACN 1130209] [ACN 1295187] [ACN 1419324] [ACN 1470131] [ACN 1490553] [ACN 1699435] [ACN 1712248] [ACN 1851899]

## Risk Assessment
The cluster consists of a member count of 10 reports, representing the complete set of documented incidents analyzed [ACN 1026406] [ACN 1111863] [ACN 1130209] [ACN 1295187] [ACN 1419324] [ACN 1470131] [ACN 1490553] [ACN 1699435] [ACN 1712248] [ACN 1851899].

* **Severity (0.90):** This score indicates a high level of operational hazard or adverse impact associated with the events described across the member reports [ACN 1026406] [ACN 1111863] [ACN 1130209] [ACN 1295187] [ACN 1419324] [ACN 1470131] [ACN 1490553] [ACN 1699435] [ACN 1712248] [ACN 1851899].
* **Frequency (0.50):** This score reflects a moderate rate of occurrence within the monitored period based on the submission volume of these events [ACN 1026406] [ACN 1111863] [ACN 1130209] [ACN 1295187] [ACN 1419324] [ACN 1470131] [ACN 1490553] [ACN 1699435] [ACN 1712248] [ACN 1851899].
* **Trend (0.50):** This score represents a neutral or steady trajectory over time, indicating neither significant escalation nor reduction across the timeline of the cluster [ACN 1026406] [ACN 1111863] [ACN 1130209] [ACN 1295187] [ACN 1419324] [ACN 1470131] [ACN 1490553] [ACN 1699435] [ACN 1712248] [ACN 1851899].
* **Total Risk (0.70):** This composite score synthesizes the high severity, moderate frequency, and steady trend into a unified deterministic risk value for the cluster [ACN 1026406] [ACN 1111863] [ACN 1130209] [ACN 1295187] [ACN 1419324] [ACN 1470131] [ACN 1490553] [ACN 1699435] [ACN 1712248] [ACN 1851899].

## Recommended Brief
General aviation flights have experienced critical losses of separation and near midair collisions, requiring sudden evasive maneuvers by flight crews [ACN 1111863, ACN 1470131, ACN 1490553]. In one instance, a flight instructor took the controls from a student, reduced power, and turned after an air traffic control advisory, observing an eastbound aircraft pass overhead with less than 300 feet of clearance [ACN 1111863]. In another event, a pilot cruising at 3,300 feet MSL took evasive action by rapidly descending to 3,000 feet to avoid crossing traffic that failed to generate an ADS-B or collision avoidance alert [ACN 1470131]. Additionally, an instructor took immediate evasive controls during an approach to land when another aircraft passed within 100 feet after being alerted over the radio [ACN 1490553].

clusters.brief:
# Draft: In-flight cabin and cockpit odor and fume events causing physiological symptoms

## Hazard
Aircraft cabin and cockpit contamination from unidentified odors, electrical fumes, or dirty-sock/mold smells can cause physiological impairment in flight crew and cabin crew, including throat/eye irritation, metallic taste, headaches, sleepiness, and fatigue [ACN 1441737] [ACN 1635960] [ACN 1648208] [ACN 1667350] [ACN 1667521] [ACN 1671682] [ACN 1835420].

## Precedent
- Flight deck and cabin crews experienced a "dirty sock" odor entering the aircraft via the ventilation system after APU start, leading to crew symptoms that required paramedic evaluation and hospital assessment for all flight attendants [ACN 1822957].
- Flight crews reported strong "dirty sock" or "wet dog" smells emerging from cockpit vents and forward cabin areas during climb and descent phases, prompting crew members to don oxygen masks and execute QRH odor procedures [ACN 1874093] [ACN 1872334].
- A mild dirty sock odor was detected isolated to the cockpit during an idle descent from 10,000 to 3,000 feet, which persisted and remained detectable by maintenance personnel upon arrival at the gate [ACN 1853717].
- Flight crews encountered musty metallic and burning plastic odors during climb out alongside cockpit smoke warnings, necessitating QRH checklist execution and an immediate precautionary return/landing [ACN 1837816].
- Flight crew members experienced pungent exhaust and metallic/oil fumes during climb out and descent, requiring donning of oxygen masks, execution of the fumes QRC/QRH, and an unscheduled diversion [ACN 1870632].

## Risk Assessment
* **Member Count (7):** The cluster is composed of 7 distinct safety event reports [ACN 1441737] [ACN 1635960] [ACN 1648208] [ACN 1667350] [ACN 1667521] [ACN 1671682] [ACN 1835420].
* **Severity (0.86):** The high severity score of 0.86 indicates that the events documented in these reports involve significant operational impact or critical safety hazards [ACN 1441737] [ACN 1635960] [ACN 1648208] [ACN 1667350] [ACN 1667521] [ACN 1671682] [ACN 1835420].
* **Frequency (0.35):** The frequency score of 0.35 reflects a moderate-to-low rate of occurrence for this specific issue relative to the broader reporting baseline [ACN 1441737] [ACN 1635960] [ACN 1648208] [ACN 1667350] [ACN 1667521] [ACN 1671682] [ACN 1835420].
* **Trend (0.64):** The trend value of 0.64 reflects an increasing or accelerating reporting pattern over time across the cluster's records [ACN 1441737] [ACN 1635960] [ACN 1648208] [ACN 1667350] [ACN 1667521] [ACN 1671682] [ACN 1835420].
* **Total Risk (0.66):** The overall composite risk score of 0.66 integrates the high severity, low-to-moderate frequency, and rising trend computed from all member records in the cluster [ACN 1441737] [ACN 1635960] [ACN 1648208] [ACN 1667350] [ACN 1667521] [ACN 1671682] [ACN 1835420].

## Recommended Brief
Brief drafting unavailable this run. [ACN 1441737] [ACN 1635960] [ACN 1648208] [ACN 1667350] [ACN 1667521] [ACN 1671682] [ACN 1835420]
### Investigator Draft: Cabin and Cockpit Contamination Events

Flight crews and cabin personnel have reported multiple inflight and ground contamination events characterized by acrid electrical odors, dirty-sock smells, sour musty burning scents, and mold-like odors [ACN 1441737] [ACN 1635960] [ACN 1648208] [ACN 1667350] [ACN 1667521] [ACN 1835420]. These odors—occasionally accompanied by visible cabin haze—have manifested across various flight phases, including boarding, climb, descent, and taxi [ACN 1441737] [ACN 1648208] [ACN 1667521] [ACN 1671682]. In several instances, the events coincided with prior fume write-ups or recent maintenance actions such as engine changes and generator issues [ACN 1635960] [ACN 1648208] [ACN 1667521].

Crew operational responses have included executing electrical fire or fumes Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) procedures, isolating master switches, donning supplemental oxygen, and coordinating communications between cabin crew and the flight deck [ACN 1635960] [ACN 1648208] [ACN 1667350] [ACN 1667521] [ACN 1835420].

Exposure to these fumes has led to acute and lingering physiological impairment among crew members [ACN 1441737] [ACN 1635960] [ACN 1648208] [ACN 1667521] [ACN 1671682]. Documented symptoms include stinging and burning eyes, raw throat irritation, coughing, loss of voice, metallic or acidic tastes, bloody nasal mucus, balance difficulties, headaches, drowsiness, and extreme fatigue [ACN 1441737] [ACN 1635960] [ACN 1648208] [ACN 1667521] [ACN 1671682].

evidence.narrative_excerpt: During boarding we noticed a sour musty burning odor coming from the gaskets in the aft galley. We notified the captain but the smell seemed to dissipate so we took the flight. Upon landing the smell returned but a lot stronger and was irritating our eyes and throats. We notified the captain by phone and told him this. The pilots left the aicraft without writing it up. I have irritation in my throat and some balance issues for 2 days now. If these do not improve I will seek medical advice.

clusters.hazard_statement: Breakdowns in visual scan, radio communication lapses, and cockpit distractions can compromise traffic separation, resulting in near midair collisions and requiring sudden evasive maneuvers (ACN 1043923, ACN 1181989, ACN 1318309, ACN 1348529, ACN 1695902, ACN 1791774).
clusters.brief:
# Draft: In-Flight Traffic Separation Conflicts and Near Midair Collisions

## Hazard
Breakdowns in visual scan, radio communication lapses, and cockpit distractions can compromise traffic separation, resulting in near midair collisions and requiring sudden evasive maneuvers (ACN 1043923, ACN 1181989, ACN 1318309, ACN 1348529, ACN 1695902, ACN 1791774). [ACN 1013497] [ACN 1043923] [ACN 1181989] [ACN 1318309] [ACN 1348529] [ACN 1695902] [ACN 1791774] [ACN 1803068]

## Precedent
- A pilot turned the radio volume down and focused visual attention on ground traffic in the run-up area, resulting in a failure to detect conflicting traffic on short final and culminating in a near midair collision and go-around [ACN 988233].
- Failure by an aircraft to utilize the radio or follow standard traffic pattern entry procedures resulted in a near-miss during initial climb-out [ACN 1119182].
- An erroneous frequency selection left a pilot unaware of landing traffic, requiring an immediate aborted takeoff and sharp evasive turn off the runway when an aircraft was spotted on short final for the opposite runway [ACN 1681937].
- Controller distraction, task saturation from multiple aircraft calling on frequency, and transponder tracking difficulties compromised traffic separation between converging aircraft at the same altitude, prompting urgent evasive turns and an immediate descent clearance below the minimum IFR altitude [ACN 1814775].
- An uncorrected ADS-B altitude discrepancy and delayed visual acquisition resulted in two aircraft passing in close proximity with only 150 feet of lateral separation [ACN 1777963].

## Risk Assessment
This cluster contains a total of 8 member reports documenting related operational events [ACN 1013497] [ACN 1043923] [ACN 1181989] [ACN 1318309] [ACN 1348529] [ACN 1695902] [ACN 1791774] [ACN 1803068].

* **Severity (0.88):** This high value indicates that the safety impacts, hazards, and potential consequences detailed across the events are substantial [ACN 1013497] [ACN 1043923] [ACN 1181989] [ACN 1318309] [ACN 1348529] [ACN 1695902] [ACN 1791774] [ACN 1803068].
* **Frequency (0.40):** This metric reflects a moderate baseline rate of occurrence represented by the 8 reports within the analyzed dataset [ACN 1013497] [ACN 1043923] [ACN 1181989] [ACN 1318309] [ACN 1348529] [ACN 1695902] [ACN 1791774] [ACN 1803068].
* **Trend (0.50):** This score denotes a neutral, stable trajectory over time, showing neither a significant increase nor a decrease in the rate of incoming reports across the cluster timeline [ACN 1013497] [ACN 1043923] [ACN 1181989] [ACN 1318309] [ACN 1348529] [ACN 1695902] [ACN 1791774] [ACN 1803068].

## Recommended Brief
Breakdowns in visual scanning, environmental hindrances such as sun glare, and cockpit distractions significantly degrade traffic separation and can force abrupt evasive maneuvers [ACN 1318309, ACN 1348529, ACN 1695902]. For instance, a pilot distracted by flight survey computers and fatigue executed an immediate climbing turn to evade oncoming traffic detected within a quarter-mile [ACN 1348529], while another flight required abrupt descending evasive action when intense sun glare hindered early visual acquisition of head-on traffic [ACN 1695902]. During training operations, lapses in visual scanning combined with unverified transponder altitude reporting modes have led to secondary radar tracking omissions and close encounters requiring military traffic to maneuver clear [ACN 1318309].

Radio communication lapses and misheard clearances also generate severe collision hazards in terminal and approach environments [ACN 1013497, ACN 1043923, ACN 1181989, ACN 1791774]. Non-compliance or failure to establish two-way communication degrades air traffic control's ability to provide timely traffic calls, contributing to occurrences such as an unidentified aircraft passing roughly 20 feet below a cruising Skyhawk [ACN 1013497, ACN 1043923]. Furthermore, low radio volume settings have led to landing approaches facing opposing-direction runway traffic [ACN 1181989], and misheard parallel runway assignments have resulted in aircraft crossing directly underneath another on final approach by a margin of only 200 feet [ACN 1791774].
